requirements.invariant: Maintain small versioned synthetic-only source fixtures that preserve known Firestore, Auth-metadata, and Storage-metadata shapes for deterministic decoding, legacy-variant, idempotency/failure, relationship-mapping, malformed/ambiguous-blocker, and reconciliation tests without a Firebase application adapter or cloud fixture environment.

The fixture bundle preserves raw source values and IDs through a closed tagged model. Integer is canonical `0|-?[1-9][0-9]*` text within Int64, rejecting plus, leading zero and negative zero. Double is exactly 16 lowercase hex IEEE-754 bits, preserving positive/negative zero, infinities and NaN payloads. Timestamp seconds use that canonical integer grammar within -62135596800...253402300799 and nanoseconds are 0...999999999. Geopoint uses two finite double-bit values whose decoded latitude is -90...90 and longitude -180...180. Bytes use padded RFC-4648 base64 whose decode/re-encode is byte-identical and decoded length is at most 1048487. Reference has an even 2...200 segment count, each segment 1...1500 UTF-8 bytes, total joined length at most 6144 bytes, and no empty/slash/NUL/dot/dot-dot segment. String values are at most 1048487 UTF-8 bytes. Map keys are at most 1500 UTF-8 bytes, unique, unnormalized and ascending by raw UTF-8 bytes; arrays retain order; each collection has at most 10000 entries. Maximum nesting depth is 20 and maximum total value nodes per payload is 50000. Valid-but-unsupported and malformed shapes remain distinct named blocker evidence rather than being dropped, coerced, normalized, transformed, or granted target meaning.

One bounded manifest envelope contains canonical content plus bundleSHA256 and excludes only that digest field from authentication. Raw manifest-envelope bytes are limited to 263168 before JSON decoding and unknown envelope/content keys fail closed. Canonical JSON uses the unchanged migration-core sorted-key/no-escaped-slash UTF-8 convention. Canonical manifest content is at most 262144 bytes; each of exactly `auth/identity-metadata.json`, `firestore/documents.json`, and `storage/object-metadata.json` is at most 4194304 bytes; aggregate payload bytes are at most 12582912; checked manifest-content-plus-payload source byteCount is at most 12845056. The bundle preimage is ASCII `ledger.firebase-source-fixture.v1` plus NUL, UInt64 big-endian manifest-content length and exact canonical manifest-content bytes, followed by the three payload tuples in ascending raw-UTF8 path order, each UInt32 big-endian path-byte length, path bytes, UInt64 big-endian payload-byte length, and exact payload bytes. Final manifest-envelope framing and bundleSHA256 bytes are not recursively included, while canonical manifest-content bytes are authenticated and included in source byteCount. MigrationSourceSnapshot.byteCount is the checked sum of canonical manifest-content and payload bytes, sha256 is the bundle digest, and exportID is its first 32 lowercase hex characters. Manifest content authenticates fixture/schema/sanitization versions, synthetic provenance, capture time, opaque Account-scope identity, exact file roles/counts/raw-payload SHA-256 values, per-entity counts/hashes, and evidence-only disposition. Each per-entity hash preimage is ASCII `ledger.firebase-source-fixture.entity.v1` plus NUL, UInt32 big-endian entity-code length and bytes, then records sorted by raw-UTF8 stable source-record ID, each framed as UInt32 ID length/bytes plus UInt64 canonical-record length/bytes; count is that exact record count. Malformed and valid-but-unsupported cases use separate stable entity codes and preserve canonical raw evidence.

Version-controlled v1 data uses synthetic IDs and values only while covering legacy enum/type variants, proto Items, movement lineage, live/paid Invoices, missing relationships, mixed categories, returns, credits, receipt-completeness cases, and metadata-only attachment references. Admission is limited to the exact reviewed v1 component and bundle digests, schema-specific prohibited identity/credential/media fields fail closed, and human privacy review is recorded against the exact committed bytes. The code does not claim it can semantically detect arbitrary PII. Restricted sanitized production-derived snapshots remain outside this package and belong to a separate restricted-snapshot workflow.

Validated fixture identity derives one exact MigrationSourceSnapshot with source_fixture environment and deterministic per-entity source hashes/counts compatible with the verified MigrationRunIntegrity plan; repeated decode/restart is byte-stable and tamper, path escape, duplicate, count/hash mismatch, noncanonical bytes, unsupported version, and oversize fail closed.

The fixture catalog and tests are provider-free migration-test evidence only. They perform no filesystem discovery beyond caller-supplied bytes, network/provider/database/Auth/Storage access, export, transform, load, reconciliation execution, hosted rehearsal, production read/write, Firebase application change, apply authorization, release, or cutover.

items: Define closed bounded fixture/version/file-role/value-kind/provenance and stable failure values without importing a provider SDK.

Represent null, bool, string, signed Int64 decimal, exact IEEE-754 bits, bounded timestamp seconds/nanoseconds, segmented document reference, finite ranged geopoint bits, canonical padded base64 bytes, ordered array and raw-UTF8-key-sorted unique map entries explicitly so JSON cannot erase Firebase source type; freeze depth, node, string/key and total-byte ceilings.

Derive only immutable source-fixture and per-entity identity using exact domain-separated length-prefixed canonical-manifest-content plus three-payload preimages compatible with verified MigrationRunIntegrity; canonical manifest content is authenticated and included in source byteCount, only final envelope framing/bundleSHA256 bytes are excluded from recursive digest/count, and the catalog performs no target transform or product classification.

items: Reject a raw manifest envelope above 263168 bytes before JSON decoding; canonical bundle and component bytes reconstruct identically across process restart with exact size/hash/count/version limits and golden preimage/digest vectors.

Reject unknown fields/kinds, invalid tagged values, duplicates/case collisions, absolute or escaping logical relative paths, manifest/file/entity mismatch, tamper, noncanonical order/bytes, and oversize without partial accepted state. Filesystem containment, lstat/no-follow, regular-file identity and TOCTOU defense belong to a separate loader slice because this core receives bytes.
Storage fixtures contain metadata and synthetic placeholder identity only; no production URL, bucket, object name, token, user media byte, download, upload, move, delete, or retention behavior.
Attachment reference/object absence, duplication, wrong bucket/namespace, thumbnail metadata and placeholder-content cases remain explicit source evidence rather than target Storage authority.

appMcp.notApplicable: Neither application links LedgerTargetMigrationCore and no MCP resource/tool or Firebase adapter is added.

items: Validated manifest produces exact source_fixture snapshot identity plus unique sorted per-entity counts and source hashes consumed by a later MigrationRunPlan.

Every source document and metadata entry is counted exactly once or retained as a named malformed/ambiguous blocker; fixture coverage is declared and never represented as complete production coverage.

Failures expose only stable bounded schema/version/kind/logical-path/count/hash/canonical/prohibited-field/catalog-mismatch codes and never fixture payload text, a raw identity, path, URL, credential, token, or provider detail.

Accepted evidence reports exact reviewed synthetic fixture/version/count/hash identity, human-review evidence reference and evidence_only disposition only; it cannot report migration, rehearsal, approval, production success or generic PII detection.
The contract and fixtures remain test-only in the separate provider-free migration module; rollback is source reversion.
Current profilers are aggregate production read-only evidence and legacy migration/ is reverse-direction history; neither may be imported, invoked, copied, or treated as a fixture schema or artifact.

verification.expected: Exact inclusive vectors prove every stated integer/double/timestamp/geopoint/base64/reference/string/key/collection/depth/node ceiling and canonical-rejection rule, including Int64 and timestamp extrema, both zero signs, finite/infinite/NaN bit patterns and payloads, coordinate endpoints, 2/200 reference segments, 1048487-byte value/decoded-byte maxima, 1500-byte key/segment maxima, 10000-entry collections, depth 20 and 50000 nodes. Valid-but-unsupported differs from malformed and normalized target values are absent.

Golden vectors prove exact domain-separated length-prefixed manifest-content, payload-tuple and per-entity preimage bytes/digests; repeated test-resource load, canonical encode, decode and restart preserve identical manifest-content-plus-payload byteCount, raw component/entity hashes, versions, capture evidence, first-32-hex exportID and source snapshot identity. Independently mutating every authenticated manifest field, path, length, payload, file hash, entity grouping/order/count/hash or bundle digest fails. Exact 263168 raw-envelope pre-decode, 262144 canonical-content, 4194304 per-payload, 12582912 aggregate-payload and 12845056 source-byteCount ceilings plus checked overflow refusal are exercised.

Unknown schema/kind/field, malformed or unsupported tagged values, duplicate/case-colliding logical paths/IDs/entities, absolute/traversing paths, changed bytes/count/hash/order/digest, noncanonical input and oversized content fail atomically. Exact reviewed catalog-digest mismatch and schema-specific prohibited identity/credential/media fields fail without claiming arbitrary-string PII detection; filesystem alias checks are explicitly outside this byte-only contract.

Synthetic metadata covers referenced, missing, duplicate, cross-bucket/namespace and thumbnail/placeholder cases without real object bytes or network access; any URL, token, production bucket/object or unreviewed byte is rejected.

The exact v1 bundle yields one source_fixture MigrationSourceSnapshot and sorted entity plans whose ID/time/byte-count/hash/count/source-hash values validate under the unchanged MigrationRunIntegrity contract; malformed/ambiguous cases remain blocker inputs and no apply or transform occurs.

Manifest totals and per-entity hashes account for every synthetic Firestore/Auth/Storage entry exactly once, named coverage limits remain explicit, and no test claims production representativeness or complete source-to-target reconciliation.

notes: READY package only; executable implementation remains unopened until the exact READY checkpoint passes immutable CI. Four independent adversarial review rounds drove corrections to executor authority, manifest/entity digest preimages, exact tagged-value and byte ceilings, synthetic-only privacy enforcement, filesystem ownership, Swift package visibility, policy/receipt canonical evidence, and one frozen scaffold phrase; final review returned GO with no P0-P3 finding. Both Swift leaves remain comment-only and all four resources remain empty schema-version-zero ready_scaffold_only markers. Package.swift copies Fixtures only into the migration test target, and the environment checker fails if a leaf becomes executable, the exact tree gains an extra/nonregular entry, or a resource departs from its empty scaffold before implementation begins. The catalog admits only exact reviewed synthetic bundle/component digests plus schema-specific prohibited-field checks and human privacy evidence; it does not claim generic PII detection. Aggregate profiler findings may enumerate test shapes but profiler code/artifacts, legacy migration/, migration/out, production data, credentials, Firebase application code, and target providers may not be reused. A separate future filesystem-loader slice owns lstat/no-follow, containment, exact enumeration, file-identity and TOCTOU guarantees. No source export, transform, load, reconciliation execution, apply, hosted rehearsal, production access, release, or cutover is authorized.
